newsitem.title: HONG KONG: CITIC to get windfall from Hongkong Telecom sale.
newsitem.headline: CITIC to get windfall from Hongkong Telecom sale.

text.p: A hefty windfall from CITIC Pacific Ltd's sale of its 7.74 percent stake in Hongkong Telecom will free the conglomerate from pressing financing needs and boost its earnings, analysts said on Friday.

"The immediate impact is the reduction in financial risk," said Steven Thompson, senior analyst at Nikko Research Center, who ramped up his 1997 earnings estimate for the red chip company to HK$9.94 billion (US$1.28 billion) from HK$5.35 billion.

CITIC Pacific said on Friday it had agreed in principle to sell its 904.69 million shares in Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd to China Everbright Holdings Co Ltd for about HK$12.60 per share or a total HK$11.4 billion.
The company's debt levels soared earlier this year when it bought a 20 percent interest in Hong Kong utility China Light & Power Co Ltd for HK$16.25 billion.

CITIC Pacific signed a HK$12.5 billion bridge loan in February to help finance the purchase and its gearing rose to about 70 percent. Analysts said the ratio could now fall to about 30 percent with the cash from the Hongkong Telecom sale.

CITIC Pacific had long been expected to slash its Hongkong Telecom stake, or sell it outright, after it reduced its holding to eight percent from 10 percent last June and said it had decided to refocus its investment strategy.
"I think CITIC was shopping around for quite some time and ended up getting the price that it wanted, which was around HK$12.60," said Andrew Fernow, director of research at Vickers Ballas.
"It is still a good gain for CITIC in terms of what its initial investment was, so you will see a gain to boost earnings for CITIC," he said.
Vickers said CITIC Pacific should earn more than HK$4.0 billion from the deal. "They will be in a position to acquire more assets," said Fernow.
But other analysts believed CITIC would use the money mainly for financing the China Light purchase.
They said CITIC had switched its investment from a relatively low growth Hongkong Telecom to China Light, which would see good earnings from property sales up until 1999.

"It probably will not pick up any more strategic investments for now since the China Light deal is quite large in size but it may buy some local property interests or projects in China," said Edward Chan, head of research at Amsteel Securities.
But he saw CITIC Pacific's major growth in the next few years in China's infrastructure projects and a recovery in trading business.

CITIC shares rose HK$0.90, or two percent, to HK$44.40 on Friday. The shares, which were suspended in the morning session, touched a year high of HK$45.40 shortly after the deal was announced in early afternoon.
